Assembly.information:
State representatives write, review and vote on legislation that becomes state law if approved by the Legislature and signed by the governor.
State representatives serve on one or more of 37 committees that take public testimony on bills and review legislation.
They work on a state budget every other year to determine how tens of billions of dollars are spent.
State representatives also oversee a small staff that helps provide constituent services. Each member of the Assembly represents roughly 59,000 people.

races.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Joel Kitchens, R-Sturgeon Bay, faces Carlton Democrat Renee Paplham in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Kitchens was first elected to the seat in 2014 and defeated Paplham in 2024 by 24 percentage points. Neither Kitchens nor Paplham faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Shae Sortwell, R-Two Rivers, faces Democrat industrial sanitation worker Alicia Saunders, of Kimberly. The district favors Republicans. Sortwell, a truck driver and former U.S. Army sergeant, was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and defeated Saunders in 2024 by 26 percentage points. Neither Sortwell nor Saunders faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Ron Tusler, R-Harrison, does not face an opponent in his reelection bid. The district favors Republicans. Tusler was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and won by 29 percentage points in 2024.

Rep. David Steffen, R-Howard, faces Democrat logistics broker Alexia Unertl, of Suamico. The district favors Republicans. Steffen was first elected to the Assembly in 2014 and won in 2024 by 32 percentage points. Neither Steffen nor Unertl faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Joy Goeben, R-Hobart, faces Democrat parks director Justin Schumacher, of Freedom, and Little Chute independent David Schupbach. The district favors Republicans. Goeben was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won by 26 percentage points in 2024.

Rep. Elijah Behnke, R-Chase, faces Democrat Shirley Hinze. The district favors Republicans. Behnke was first elected to the Assembly in 2021 and defeated Hinze in 2024 by 34 percentage points. Neither Behnke nor Hinze faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Karen Kirsch, D-Greenfield, faces Republican Lee Whiting. The district favors Democrats. Kirsch was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 when she defeated Whiting by 17 percentage points. Neither Kirsch nor Whiting faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Sylvia Ortiz-Velez, D-Milwaukee, faces Democrat case manager Ismael Luna in the primary. Whoever wins will face Republican Angel Sanchez, of Milwaukee in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Ortiz-Velez was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won unopposed with 98% of the vote in 2024. Ortiz-Velez was charged with disorderly conduct in February regarding a 2025 legislative feud stemming from her alleged exclusion in the drafting of resolutions honoring Hispanics. Wisconsin Democrats said Ortiz-Velez threatened to shoot three Democratic caucus members over disagreements, and she announced her departure from the caucus shortly after. She pleaded no contest in March.

Rep. Priscilla Prado, D-Milwaukee, faces Democrat Mimi Reza in the primary. Whoever wins will go against Republican Samuel Guerrero, who did not face a primary opponent. The district favors Democrats. Prado was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by 40 percentage points.

Rep. Darrin Madison, D-Milwaukee, faces Green Party retiree Robert Longwell-Grice, of Shorewood. The district favors Democrats. Madison, a founding member of the Wisconsin State Assembly’s Socialist Caucus, was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won unopposed with 99% of the vote in 2024. Neither Madison nor Longwell-Grice faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Sequanna Taylor, D-Milwaukee, faces Republican business owner Shandowlyon Reaves, of Milwaukee. The district favors Democrats. Taylor was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won unopposed with 99% of the vote. Neither Taylor nor Reaves faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Russell Antonio Goodwin Sr., D-Milwaukee, faces Milwaukee consultant Jordan Roman in the Democratic primary. The district favors Democrats. Goodwin was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won unopposed with 80% of the vote. No Republicans filed to run in the 12th District, which means the primary winner is expected to win in November.

Wauwatosa attorney David Sanchez Brookfield and consultant Amy Zimmerman are running in the Democratic primary. The winner will face Republican marketing consultant Mike Morgan, of Wauwatosa, in the general election. The seat is currently held by Democrat state Rep. Robyn Vining, of Wauwatosa, who is not seeking reelection and is instead running for the 5th state Senate District.

Rep. Angelito Tenorio, D-West Allis, faces Republican AmyRose Murphy, of West Allis. Tenorio was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by 9 percentage points. Neither Tenorio nor Murphy faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Adam Neylon, R-Pewaukee, faces Pewaukee Democrat Stephen Tryon. The district favors Republicans. Neylon was first elected to the Assembly in 2013 and won reelection in 2024 by 18 percentage points. Neither Neylon nor Tryon faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Kalan Haywood, D-Milwaukee, faces Republican Alciro Deacon, of Milwaukee. The district favors Democrats. Haywood, the assistant minority leader, was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and won unopposed with 99% of the vote in 2024. Neither Haywood nor Deacon faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Supreme Moore Omokunde, D-Milwaukee, faces Republican entrepreneur Charlene Abughrin, of Milwaukee. The district favors Democrats. Moore Omokunde was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won unopposed with 98% of the vote in 2024. Neither Moore Omokunde nor Abughrin faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Margaret Arney, D-Wauwatosa, faces Republican Joel Richmond. The district favors Democrats. Arney was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by 64 percentage points. Neither Arney nor Richmond faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Ryan Clancy, D-Milwaukee, faces Democrat shopkeeper Bridget Maniaci in the Democratic primary. Clancy was one of two founding members of the Wisconsin State Assembly’s Socialist Caucus and is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America. Maniaci is running as a progressive Democrat. Whoever wins will face Milwaukee Republican Yasmine Outlaw in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Clancy was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won unopposed with 98% of the vote in 2024.

Rep. Christine Sinicki, D-Milwaukee, faces Republican Kyle Cleary. The district favors Democrats. Sinicki was first elected to the Assembly in 1998 and won by 22 percentage points in 2024. Neither Sinicki nor Cleary faced a primary opponent.

Oak Creek Mayor Dan Bukiewicz faces Milwaukee retired community organizer David Liners in the Democratic primary election. The winner will face Carroll University student Dylan Pfaffenbach, a Republican, in the general election. Pfaffenbach did not face a primary challenge. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Jessie Rodriguez, who does not seek reelection. Rodriguez narrowly won the district in 2024 by three percentage points, and Democrats are targeting the seat this year to flip the Assembly.

Rep. Paul Melotik, R-Grafton, faces Democrat educator Dana Glasstein, of Mequon. The district favors Republicans. Melotik was first elected in a 2023 special election and defeated Glasstein in 2024 by 16 percentage points. Neither Melotik nor Glasstein faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Deb Andraca, D-Whitefish Bay, faces Republican Aleaner Pabonnie. The district favors Democrats. Andraca, a member of the Joint Finance Committee, was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won by 25 percentage points in 2024. Neither Andraca nor Pabonnie faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Dan Knodl, R-Germantown, faces Democrat Matt Brown. The district favors Republicans. Knodl was first elected to the Assembly in 2008 and went on to serve in the state Senate after a 2023 special election. He was reelected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by 20 percentage points. Neither Knodl nor Brown faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Paul Tittl, R-Manitowoc, faces Democrat retired teacher Christopher Able, of Manitowoc. The district favors Republicans. Tittl, an owner of the Vacuum & Sewing Center in Manitowoc, was first elected to the Assembly in 2012 and won by 24 percentage points in 2024. Neither Tittl nor Able faced a primary opponent.

Tyler Schneekloth, of Wilson, former Sheboygan Alderman John Belanger and James Brotz are running in the Republican primary. The winner will face Rep. Joe Sheehan, D-Sheboygan, in the general election. Sheehan did not face a primary opponent. Sheehan was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 where he narrowly won the seat by 3 percentage points and knocked out a Republican incumbent. It’s a seat Republicans are hoping to retake as they also try to hold on to their majority in the chamber.

Rep. Lindee Brill, R-Sheboygan Falls, is unopposed in the primary and general elections. The district favors Republicans. Brill was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by 35 percentage points.

Rep. Rob Kreibich, R-New Richmond, faces Democrat Robin Lillesve. The district favors Republicans. Kreibich was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by 32 percentage points. Neither Kreibich nor Lillesve faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Treig Pronschinske, R-Mondovi, faces former Rep. Chris Danou, D-Trempealeau. The district favors Republicans. Pronschinske first defeated Danou in 2016 and won by 30 percentage points in 2024. Neither Pronschinske nor Danou faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Shannon Zimmerman, R-River Falls, faces Democrat retired educator Kevin Knoke. Zimmerman, a member of the powerful Joint Finance Committee, was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and won the seat in 2024 by nine percentage points. Democrats are targeting this seat as they try to flip the Assembly. Neither Zimmerman nor Knoke faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Tyler August, R-Walworth, faces Democrat pediatrician John Perryman, of Williams Bay, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. August, the Assembly majority leader, was first elected to the Assembly in 2010 and won reelection in 2024 by 27 percentage points. Neither August nor Perryman faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Amanda Nedweski, R-Pleasant Prairie, faces Democrat Greg Miller. The district favors Republicans. Nedweski was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won reelection in 2024 by 36 percentage points. Neither Nedweski nor Miller faced a primary opponent.

Rick Stacey, who works in logistics, and business owner Steve Wicklund will face off in the Republican primary to determine who will compete against the winner of the Democratic primary between bookkeeper Maria Elena Bisabarros and retiree Rick Bailey. The seat is currently held by longtime Republican Speaker Robin Vos, of Rochester, who is not seeking reelection. The district favors Republicans. Vos was reelected in 2024 by 27 percentage points.

Rep. Rob Swearingen, R-Rhinelander, faces Democrat Merlin Van Buren. The district favors Republicans. Swearingen was first elected to the Assembly in 2012 and won reelection in 2024 by 28 percentage points. Neither Swearingen nor Van Buren faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Calvin Callahan, R-Tomahawk, faces Democrat educator Elizabeth McCrank, of Merrill. The district favors Republicans. Callahan was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and defeated McCrank in 2024 by 36 percentage points. Neither Callahan nor McCrank faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Jeffrey Mursau, R-Crivitz, faces independent Shena Chapman in the general election race for the 36th District. The district favors Republicans. Mursau was first elected to the Assembly in 2004 and won reelection in 2024 by 42 percentage points. No Democrat filed to run and Mursau did not face a primary opponent.

Rep. Mark Born, R-Beaver Dam, faces a challenge from Republican Steve Rydzewski, of Beaver Dam. The winner will face Democrat educator LaToya Bates, of Mayville. Bates did not face a primary opponent. The district favors Republicans. Born, a co-chair of the powerful Joint Finance Committee, was first elected to the Assembly in 2012 and defeated Bates in 2024 by 37 percentage points.

Rep. William Penterman, R-Hustisford, faces Democrat nurse Terri Wenkman, of Jefferson. The district favors Republicans. Penterman was first elected to the Assembly in 2021 and won reelection in 2024 by 35 percentage points. Neither Penterman nor Wenkman faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Alex Dallman, R-Markesan, faces Democrat small business owner Michael Skivington, of the Town of Green Lake. The district favors Republicans. Dallman was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won reelection in 2024 by 39 percentage points. Neither Dallman nor Skivington faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Karen DeSanto, D-Baraboo, faces Republican Julie Helmer. DeSanto was first elected to the Assembly in 2024, defeating Helmer’s husband, Jerry, by 8 percentage points. Neither DeSanto nor Helmer faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Tony Kurtz, R-Wonewoc, faces Democrat project manager Zach Commons, of Reedsburg. The district favors Republicans. Kurtz, a member of the Joint Finance Committee and veteran, was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and won reelection in 2024 by 26 percentage points. Neither Kurtz nor Commons faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Maureen McCarville, D-DeForest, faces Republican Keith F. Miller in the general election. The district favors Democrats. McCarville was first elected to the Assembly in 2024, winning the seat by 10 percentage points. Neither McCarville nor Miller faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Brienne Brown, D-Whitewater, faces Republican Paul McGraw. Brown was first elected to the Assembly in 2024, narrowly winning the seat by 3 percentage points. Neither Brown nor McGraw faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Ann Roe, D-Janesville, faces Republican Ron Woodman in the general election for the 44th Assembly District. The district favors Democrats. Roe was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won the seat by 13 percentage points. Neither Roe nor Woodman faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Clinton Anderson, D-Beloit, faces Republican Jocelyn Jordan. Anderson was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and ran unopposed in 2024 under the new legislative maps, winning with 96% of the vote. Neither Anderson nor Jordan faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Joan Fitzgerald, D-Fort Atkinson, faces Republican veteran John Donohue, of Fort Atkinson, in the general election. Fitzgerald was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won the seat by 5 percentage points. Neither Fitzgerald nor Donohue faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Randy Udell, D-Fitchburg, faces Republican Sandy Bakk. The district favors Democrats. Udell, the treasurer of the Democratic Party of Wisconsin, was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and ran unopposed under the new legislative maps, winning with 98% of the vote. Neither Udell nor Bakk faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Andrew Hysell, D-Sun Prairie, faces Republican retired farmer Mark Kjorlie, of the Town of York. The district favors Democrats. Hysell was first elected to the Assembly in 2024, winning the seat by 35 percentage points. Neither Hysell nor Kjorlie faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Travis Tranel, R-Cuba City, faces Democrat John Rindy, of Potosi. The district favors Republicans. Tranel was first elected to the Assembly in 2010 and won reelection in 2024 by 26 percentage points. Neither Tranel nor Rindy faced a primary opponent.

Nurse Bryna Caves, professor Bill Oemichen and Josh Mittness, who works in customer service, will face off in the Democratic primary to determine who will compete against Republican Jon Aleckson in the general election. The seat is currently held by Democrat state Rep. Jenna Jacobson, of Oregon, who is running for Senate. The district favors Democrats. Jacobson was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won reelection in 2024 by 13 percentage points. Aleckson will not face a primary opponent.

Rep. Todd Novak, R-Dodgeville, Democrat Ben Gruber, of Arena, and American Solidarity Party candidate Nathan Tataje, of Arena, will compete in the general election. Novak was first elected to the Assembly in 2014 and has survived several Democratic challenges in past elections, including in 2024 when he won reelection by just over 3 percentage points. Novak is again a target for Assembly Democrats this fall. Novak, Gruber and Tataje did not face primary opponents.

Rep. Lee Snodgrass, D-Appleton, faces Republican small business owner Reive Pullen, of Appleton. The district favors Democrats. Snodgrass was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won reelection in 2024 by 14 percentage points. Neither Snodgrass nor Pullen faced a primary opponent.

Republican Air Force veteran David Daniels, Democrat teacher Becky Nichols and independent drone pilot Rachael Dowling will face off in the general election. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Dean R. Kaufert, of Neenah, who is not seeking reelection. Democrats are targeting this seat as they seek a majority in the Assembly this fall. Kaufert won the seat in 2024 by one percentage point. Dowling, Nichols and Daniels did not face primary opponents.

Rep. Lori Palmeri, D-Oshkosh, faces Republican National Guard veteran Tim Paterson. Palmeri was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and defeated Paterson in 2024 by five percentage points. Neither Palmeri nor Paterson faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Nate Gustafson, R-Omro, faces Democrat attorney and social worker Alex Corrigan, of Clayton. The district favors Republicans. Gustafson was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won reelection in 2024 by 21 percentage points. Neither Gustafson nor Corrigan faced a primary opponent.

Self-employed Grace Abitz and forklift operator Shawna Riley will face off in the Democratic primary to determine who will compete against Republican oncologist Anthony W. Phillips in the general election. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Dave Murphy, of Hortonville, who is not seeking reelection. The district favors Republicans. Murphy was first elected to the Assembly in 2012 and won reelection in 2024 by 29 percentage points. Phillips did not face a primary opponent.

Business owner Dylan Testin, author and former state Rep. Bill Lorge, dairy farmer Kevin Krentz and Waushara County Board Supervisor Ed Delgado will face off in the Republican primary. The winner will face Democrat bartender and custodian Joey Marschall in the general election. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Kevin Petersen who is not seeking reelection. The district favors Republicans. Petersen was first elected to the Assembly in 2006 and won reelection in 2024 by 34 percentage points. Marschall did not face a primary opponent.

Washington County Board Supervisor Christopher D. Bossert and president of Common Sense Citizens of Washington County Bernie Newman will face off in the Republican primary to determine who will compete against West Bend Democrat Dennis D. Degenhardt in the general election. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Rick Gundrum who is not seeking reelection. The district favors Republicans. Gundrum was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and won reelection in 2024 by 43 percentage points. Degenhardt did not face a primary opponent.

Republican Bradley Peterson faces Democrat retired teacher Jack Holzman. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Robert Brooks who is not seeking reelection. The district favors Republicans. Brooks was first elected to the Assembly in 2014 and defeated Holzman in 2024 by 52 percentage points. Neither Holzman nor Peterson faced a primary opponent.

Republican prosthetist and orthotic fitter Marty Ryan, of Fond du Lac, faces independent substitute teacher Tiffany Brault, of Fond du Lac, in the general election. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Jerry O’Connor who is not seeking reelection. The district favors Republicans. O’Connor was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won reelection in 2024 by 20 percentage points. No Democrats filed to run in the district and Ryan did not face a primary opponent.

Veteran Ben Brist, pharmacist Brian Bock and business owner Lawanda Chambers will face off in the Democratic primary to determine who will compete against Rep. Bob Donovan, R-Greenfield. The district is one of the races Democrats are targeting to regain control of the Assembly this fall. Donovan was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and narrowly won reelection in 2024 by 3 percentage points. Donovan does not face a primary opponent.

Rep. Angelina M. Cruz, D-Racine, faces Republican business owner Mike Bellagio, of Racine. The district favors Democrats. Cruz was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 when she ran unopposed, winning with 95% of the vote. Neither Cruz nor Bellagio faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Robert Wittke, R-Caledonia, faces Democrat business owner Eddie Phanichkul, of Greendale. Wittke was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and ran unopposed in 2024 under the new legislative maps, winning with 97% of the vote. Neither Wittke nor Phanichkul faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Tip McGuire, D-Kenosha, faces Republican small business owner Ed Hibsch. McGuire, a member of the powerful Joint Finance Committee, was first elected to the Assembly in 2019 and defeated Hibsch in 2024 by 11 percentage points. Neither McGuire nor Hibsch faced a primary opponent in August.

Rep. Ben DeSmidt, D-Kenosha, faces Republican Valerie Kretchmer. DeSmidt was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won by seven percentage points. Neither DeSmidt nor Kretchmer faced a primary opponent.

Minority Leader Rep. Greta Neubauer, D-Racine, faces Republican Gina Cefalu Paulick, of Racine. Neubauer was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and won reelection in 2024 by eight percentage points. Neither Neubauer nor Paulick faced a primary opponent.

Rep. David Armstrong, R-Rice Lake, faces Democrat small business owner, substitute teacher and high school golf coach Indiana Thompson, of Chetek. The district favors Republicans. Armstrong was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won reelection in 2024 by 35 percentage points. Neither Armstrong nor Thompson faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Rob Summerfield, R-Bloomer, faces Park Falls Democrat Elisha King, who works in manufacturing, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Summerfield was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and won reelection in 2024 by 46 percentage points. Neither Summerfield nor King faced a primary opponent.

The race for this Assembly District is a rematch from 2024. Rep. Karen Hurd, R-Town of Withee, faces Stanley Democrat Roger Halls and Eaton independent Josh Kelley in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Hurd was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and defeated Halls and Kelley in 2024 with 71% of the vote. Hurd, Halls and Kelley didn’t face primary opponents.

Rep. Nancy VanderMeer, R-Tomah, faces Democrat writer and educator Stephanie Stuve Bodeen, of Black River Falls, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. VanderMeer was first elected to the Assembly in 2014 and won reelection in 2024 by 34 percentage points. Neither VanderMeer nor Bodeen faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Vinnie Miresse, D-Stevens Point, faces Republican small business owner Jeff Disher, of Stevens Point, in the general election. Miresse was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and won the seat by six percentage points. Neither Miresse nor Disher faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Scott Krug, R-Rome, faces Democrat systems engineer Christine Maltese, of Wood County, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Krug was first elected to the Assembly in 2010 and won reelection in 2024 by 28 percentage points. Neither Krug nor Maltese faced a primary opponent.

The race for this Assembly District is a rematch from 2024. Rep. Angela Stroud, D-Ashland, faces Republican Air Force Veteran Frank Kostka, of Ashland, in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Stroud was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and defeated Kostka by 17 percentage points. Neither Stroud nor Kostka faced a primary opponent in August.

Rep. Chanz Green, R-Mason, and Republican Army veteran Scott Harbidge will face off in the August primary to determine who will compete against Democrat Paul Johnson. The district favors Republicans. Green was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won reelection in 2024 by 25 percentage points. Johnson does not face a primary opponent.

Rep. Duke Tucker, R-Town of West Marshland, faces Democrat operations manager Keith Mogel, of Wood River, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Tucker was first elected to the seat in 2024 and won the seat by 33 percentage points. Neither Tucker nor Mogel faced a primary opponent.

Five Democrats face off in the August primary for the Madison-based seat currently held by state Rep. Francesca Hong, D-Madison, who is running for governor. They include policy director Isaia Ben-Ami, Madison City Council member Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford, swim instructor and bartender Juliana Bennett, audio producer and writer Zoe Sullivan and musician Tony Castañeda. The winner of the Democratic primary will compete against Republican Nina Chat in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Hong ran unopposed in 2024 under the new legislative maps. Chat does not have a primary opponent.

Rep. Renuka Mayadev, D-Madison, faces Republican interior designer and real estate broker Jane McCormick, of the Village of Shorewood Hills, in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Mayadev was first elected to the Assembly in 2024 and ran unopposed under the new legislative maps enacted that year. Neither Mayadev nor McCormick faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Shelia Stubbs, D-Madison, faces Republican Henry Johnson in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Stubbs was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and ran unopposed in 2024 under the state’s new legislative maps. Neither Stubbs nor Johnson faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Lisa Subeck, D-Madison, faces Republican writer John Fons, of Madison, in the general election. The district covering Madison’s west side favors Democrats. Subeck was first elected to the Assembly in 2014 and ran unopposed in 2024 under the state’s new legislative maps. Neither Subeck nor Fons faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Mike Bare, D-Verona, faces Madison Republican Simran Arora in the general election. The district favors Democrats. Bare was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won reelection in 2024 by 47 percentage points. Neither Bare nor Arora faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Alex Joers, D-Town of Westport, faces Republican Mark S. Maier in the general election. Joers was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and ran unopposed in 2024 under the state’s new legislative maps. Neither Joers nor Maier faced a primary opponent.

Republican supply chain analyst Bryson Reyes, of Waukesha, faces Democrat Waukesha City Council member Rico Camacho in the general election for the 82nd Assembly District. The seat is currently held by Republican state Rep. Scott Allen, R-Waukesha, who is not seeking reelection. The district leans toward Republicans, but saw a Democrat win the Waukesha mayor’s race in this year’s April elections. Allen was first elected to the Assembly in 2014 and won reelection in 2024 by 14 percentage points. Neither Reyes nor Camacho faced a primary opponent.
Rep. Dave Maxey, R-New Berlin, is running unopposed in the primary and general elections. Maxey was first elected to the Assembly in 2022 and won by 22 percentage points in 2024.
Rep. Chuck Wichgers, R-Muskego, is running unopposed in the primary and general elections. He was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and won by 44 percentage points in 2024.

Rep. Patrick Snyder, R-Weston, faces Democrat energy efficiency professional John Kroll, of Wausau, in the general election. The district leans toward Republicans and is a seat to watch as Democrats are targeting to win a majority in the Assembly in November. Snyder was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and won reelection in 2024 by 6 percentage points. Neither Snyder nor Kroll faced a primary opponent.

Rep. John Spiros, R-Marshfield, faces Democrat electrical contractor Andy Wuethrich, of Arpin, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Spiros, an Air Force veteran, was first elected to the Assembly in 2012 and won reelection in 2024 by 34 percentage points. Neither Spiros nor Wuethrich faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Brent Jacobson, R-Mosinee, faces Democrat retired broadcaster Bob Look, of Rothschild, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Jacobson was first elected to the seat in 2024 and won by 32 percentage points. Neither Jacobson nor Look faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Ben Franklin, R-De Pere, faces Democrat accounting manager Brandy Tollefson, of De Pere, in the general election. The district is a toss-up seat and a race to watch as Democrats and Republicans compete for control of the Assembly. Franklin was first elected to the seat in 2024, narrowly winning by less than one percentage point. Neither Franklin nor Tollefson faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Ryan Spaude, D-Ashwaubenon, faces Republican Marine Corps veteran Bobby R. Lindsey, of Green Bay, in the general election. It’s a key race to watch as Democrats and Republicans compete for control of the Assembly. Spaude was first elected to the seat in 2024 and won by 3 percentage points. Neither Spaude nor Lindsey faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Amaad Rivera-Wagner, D-Green Bay, faces Republican Jessica Henderson in the general election. Rivera-Wagner was first elected to the seat in 2024 and defeated Henderson by 5 percentage points. Neither Rivera-Wagner nor Henderson faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Jodi Emerson, D-Eau Claire, faces Republican business owner Bruce Stabenow in the general election. The district is one of the races to watch as Democrats and Republicans compete for control of the Assembly in November. Emerson was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and won reelection in 2024 by 3 percentage points. Neither Emerson nor Stabenow faced a primary opponent.

Fish farm owner Jeremiah Fredrickson, of Elk Mound, and Mel M. Marin will face off in the Democratic primary. The winner will face Rep. Clint Moses, R-Menomonie. Moses was first elected to the Assembly in 2020 and won reelection in 2024 by 7 percentage points. Democrats are looking to unseat Moses and flip this district for control of the Assembly in the fall. Moses did not face a primary opponent.

Rep. Christian Phelps, D-Eau Claire, faces Republican Michael Ayala in the general election. Phelps was first elected to the seat in 2024, winning by 6 percentage points. Neither Phelps nor Ayala faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Steve Doyle, D-Onalaska, faces Republican Army veteran Keith Purnell in the general election. Doyle narrowly won reelection in 2024 by less than 250 votes at the same time President Donald Trump won in the district. Doyle was first elected to the Assembly in 2011. Republicans are looking to flip the seat to retain control of the Assembly. Neither Doyle nor Purnell faced a primary opponent.

Rep. Jill Billings, D-La Crosse, faces Sparta Republican dairy farmer Cedric Schnitzler and La Crosse independent Paul Michael Weber in the general election. Billings was first elected to the Assembly in 2011 and narrowly won reelection in 2024 when she defeated Schnitzler by 4 percentage points. It’s a race to watch as Republicans and Democrats compete for control of the Assembly this fall. Billings, Schnitzler and Weber didn’t face a primary opponent.

Rep. Tara Johnson, D-Town of Shelby, faces Republican Jim Green in the general election. Johnson was first elected to the seat in 2024 and narrowly defeated former Republican state Rep. Loren Oldenburg by 2 percentage points. It’s a race to watch as Republicans and Democrats compete for control of the Assembly this fall. Neither Johnson nor Green faced a primary opponent.
Rep. Cindi Duchow, R-Town of Delafield, is running unopposed in the primary and general elections. She was first elected to the Assembly in 2015 and won in 2024 by 42 percentage points.

Rep. Jim Piwowarczyk, R-Hubertus, faces Democrat stay-at-home dad Matt Philibert, of Colgate, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Piwowarczyk was first elected to the seat in 2024 and won by 42 percentage points. Neither Piwowarczyk nor Philibert faced a primary opponent.
Rep. Barbara Dittrich, R-Oconomowoc, is running unopposed in the primary and general elections. She was first elected to the Assembly in 2018 and won unopposed in 2024 with 98% of the vote.

Senate.information:
State senators write, review and vote on legislation that becomes state law if approved by the Legislature and signed by the governor.
They vet some political appointees made by the governor, including cabinet secretaries.
Senators serve on one or more of 20 committees that take public testimony on bills and review legislation.
They work on a state budget every other year to determine how tens of billions of dollars are spent.
Senators also oversee a staff that helps provide constituent services. Each member of the state Senate represents roughly 175,000 people.

races.district-race-nutshell: Calumet County farmer Barbara Bittner, Sturgeon Bay farmer Jacob VandenPlas, Delta Defense director Katie Baney, of De Pere, and Army veteran Nic Cravillion, of New Franken, are competing in the Republican primary. Whoever wins will face Luxembourg business owner independent Mark Becker, who is the former chair of the Republican Party of Brown County. There are no Democrats running in this district. The seat is currently held by Republican Sen. André Jacque, of New Franken, who is not seeking reelection.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.
Sen. Tim Carpenter, D-Milwaukee, does not face an opponent as he seeks reelection. Carpenter was first elected in 2002.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

Rep. Robyn Vining, D-Wauwatosa, faces Pewaukee business owner Republican Mike Roberts in the race. It’s one of the top seats Senate Democrats are looking to flip as they try to win a majority this year. Kamala Harris won the district in the 2024 presidential race. Incumbent Sen. Rob Hutton, R-Brookfield, is not seeking reelection. Neither Vining nor Roberts faced a primary opponent.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.
Sen. Chris Larson, D-Milwaukee, faces Republican business owner Mike Moeller, of South Milwaukee. Larson was first elected in 2010. Neither Larson nor Moeller faced a primary opponent.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

Former state Rep. Amy Binsfield, R-Sheboygan, faces independent business owner Christian Ellis, of Sheboygan Falls. Binsfield did not face a primary opponent and no Democrats filed to run. The seat is currently held by Republican Senate Majority Leader Devin LeMahieu, of Oostburg, who is not seeking reelection.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

East Troy software developer Adam Duda faces Steven Doelder, of Bloomfield, in the Democratic primary. Bristol operations superintendent Sandy Wiedmeyer, former state Rep. Ellen Schutt, of Clinton, and Delavan investor Nick Polce are running in the Republican primary. The seat is currently held by Republican state Sen. Steven Nass, who is not seeking reelection.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.
State Sen. John Jagler, R-Watertown, faces Democrat teacher Sasha Ripley, of Packwaukee. Neither Jagler nor Ripley faced a primary opponent. Jagler was first elected to the seat in 2021.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

State Sen. Mark Spreitzer, D-Beloit, faces Republican Johnstown Supervisor Scott Fleming and process server and third-party candidate Christopher Dean, of Center Township, in the general election. None of the candidates faced primary opponents. Spreitzer was elected to the seat in 2022.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

State Rep. Jenna Jacobson, D-Oregon, childcare consultant Corrine Hendrickson, of New Glarus, and Lisa White, of Potosi, are running in the Democratic primary. The winner will face state Sen. Howard Marklein, R-Spring Green, in the general election. Marklein, one of the co-chairs of the powerful Joint Finance Committee, was elected to the seat in 2014. The 17th District is viewed as a potential flip opportunity by Senate Democrats as Kamala Harris and U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin won the district in 2024.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

State Sen. Rachael Cabral-Guevara, R-Fox Crossing, faces Democrat Emily Tseffos, of Appleton, in the general election. Neither Cabral-Guevara nor Tseffos faced a primary opponent. Cabral-Guevara, a nurse practitioner and the owner of Nurse Practitioner Health Services, was elected to the seat in 2022.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

Transit director Trevor Jung, a Racine Democrat, faces Jim Croft, a Racine Republican, in the general election. Neither Jung nor Croft faced a primary opponent. The seat is currently held by Republican state Sen. Van Wanggaard, who is not seeking reelection. The 21st District is viewed as a potential flip opportunity for Senate Democrats, as Kamala Harris and U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin won the district in 2024.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

Jeff Foster, of Grant Township, faces Richard Pulcher, of Lublin, in the Democratic primary. The winner will face state Sen. Romaine Quinn, R-Birchwood. Quinn was elected to the 25th Senate District in 2022 but now runs in the 23rd after new legislative maps were signed into law in 2024. The seat is currently held by Republican state Sen. Jesse James, who did not seek reelection.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

Former Republican state Reps. Erik Severson and Angie Sapik face off in the 25th Senate District Republican primary. The winner will face Bayfield County Board member and Democrat Charly Ray in the general election. The seat is currently held by Republican state Sen. Romaine Quinn, who is seeking election in the 23rd Senate District due to new legislative maps drawn in 2024.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.
Senate Minority Leader Dianne Hesselbein, D-Middleton, does not face an opponent. Hesselbein was elected to the Senate in 2022 and became minority leader in 2023.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

State Sen. Cory Tomczyk, R-Mosinee, faces Wausau Democrat Gillian Battino in the general election. Neither Tomczyk nor Battino faced a primary opponent. Tomczyk, who owns Industrial Recyclers of Wisconsin, was elected to the seat in 2022.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

State Sen. Jeff Smith, D-Brunswick, faces Republican Eau Claire County Supervisor Michele Magadance Skinner. Neither Smith nor Skinner faced a primary opponent. Smith was first elected to the Senate in 2018 and became assistant minority leader in 2023. The 31st District is a key race for control of the chamber. Smith won reelection in 2022 with a 1% margin, before new legislative maps were signed into law. Kamala Harris and U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin won in the new boundaries in 2024.
This seat is not up for election until 2028.

State Sen. Chris Kapenga, R-Delafield, faces Delafield attorney and Democrat Mike Van Someren in the general election. Neither Kapenga nor Van Someren faced a primary opponent. Kapenga was first elected to the Senate in 2015.

Former state Young Democrats Chair Lorenzo Santos, Milwaukee City Council member Peter Burgelis, ER nurse Mitchell Berman and Whitewater Unified School District Vice President Miguel Aranda will all face off in the Democratic primary for the 1st Congressional District. Whoever wins will challenge Republican incumbent Bryan Steil, who is endorsed by President Donald Trump, in the general election. Democrats are looking to flip the seat as a key district in taking the House. Steil was first elected to the seat in 2018 and won by 10 percentage points in 2024.

U.S. Rep. Mark Pocan, of Madison, faces Douglas Alexander, of Madison in the Democratic primary for the 2nd Congressional District. There is no Republican challenger. The district favors Democrats. Pocan was first elected to the seat in 2012 and won by 40 percentage points in 2024.

Rebecca Cooke, the 2024 Democratic nominee, faces Eau Claire counselor Emily Berge in the Democratic primary for the 3rd Congressional District. The winner will face Republican U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden in the general election, a race that could determine control of the U.S. House of Representatives. Alexander Kent, of La Crosse, and Pepin CNA Rustin Provance are also running in the general election as independent candidates. Van Orden was first elected to the seat in 2022 and defeated Cooke in 2024 by 3 percentage points.

U.S. Rep. Gwen Moore, of Milwaukee, faces genetic counselor Amy Donahue, of Milwaukee, in the Democratic primary for the 4th Congressional District. Purnima Nath and Tim Rogers are running in the Republican primary. The two primary winners will compete with independent Arthur Burks in the general election. The Milwaukee-focused district heavily favors Democrats. Moore was elected to the seat in 2004 and defeated Rogers by 53 percentage points in 2024.

Republican U.S. Rep. Scott Fitzgerald, of Clyman, faces West Bend Democrat Andrew Beck, who works in sales, for the 5th Congressional District. Neither Fitzgerald nor Beck faced a primary opponent. The district favors Republicans. Fitzgerald was elected to the seat in 2020 and won by 29 percentage points in 2024.

Wyocena substitute teacher Amanda Bell and Mequon business owner Brad Smith are running in the Democratic primary for the 6th Congressional District. The winner will face incumbent Republican U.S. Rep. Glenn Grothman, of Greenbush, in the general election. Green Party candidate Mequon business owner Matthew Arndt is also running in the general election as are independent candidates Mequon firefighter Mike Thurow and Neenah phlebotomist Elizabeth Fitzgibbon. The district favors Republicans. Grothman is endorsed by President Donald Trump. Grothman was elected to the seat in 2015 and won by 22 percentage points in 2024.

Wausau financial adviser Kevin Hermening, Superior contractor Don Raihala, Chippewa County manufacturing worker Jessi Ebben, Crescent business owner Niina Baum and Michael Alfonso are competing in the 7th Congressional District Republican primary. Alfonso is endorsed by President Donald Trump and is the son-in-law of Department of Transportation Secretary and former U.S. Rep. Sean Duffy. Former state Rep. Fred Clark, of Bayfield, New Lisbon attorney Ginger Murray and New Richmond IT consultant Chris Armstrong are facing off in the Democratic primary. The safe Republican seat is being vacated by Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany.

Mark Scheffler, of Appleton, musician Katrina deVille, of Appleton, and Green Bay Army veteran Rick Crosson are running in the 8th Congressional District Democratic primary. Whoever wins will face Republican U.S. Rep. Tony Wied, of De Pere, in the general election. The district favors Republicans. Wied is endorsed by President Donald Trump and was elected to the seat in 2024 by 14 percentage points.

Governor.information:
Wisconsin’s governor is the state’s top executive. The governor considers all bills approved by the Legislature and has the power to sign, veto, or, in the case of appropriation bills, partially veto proposed legislation that comes to their desk. They can also call the Legislature into special sessions and ask lawmakers to consider specific types of legislation.
The governor appoints heads of executive agencies, such as the Department of Natural Resources, and many state boards and commissions. Most appointees require Senate confirmation.
The governor can also make appointments to vacant judicial seats and county-level offices.
Wisconsin’s governor has the power to pardon or grant clemency for individuals in the state’s criminal justice system.
The governor is the commander in chief of the Wisconsin National Guard and can decide if and when to deploy soldiers.

races.district-race-nutshell: Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany faces Andy Manske, a 27-year-old medical services technician from Greenfield, in the race to become the GOP gubernatorial nominee. Tiffany, who is endorsed by President Donald Trump and the Republican Party of Wisconsin, is favored to win the primary election. The winner will face the candidate that wins the six-way Democratic primary on Aug. 11.

races.district-race-nutshell: After Democratic Gov. Tony Evers chose not to seek reelection this year, four candidates are running for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination. They include former Department of Administration Secretary Joel Brennan, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, Madison state Rep. Francesca Hong and Madison state Sen. Kelda Roys. The candidate that wins on Aug. 11 will face the winner of the Republican primary. Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez and former Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. CEO Missy Hughes will still appear on the ballot. Hughes dropped out of the race in June. Rodriguez exited in mid-July due to campaign fundraising problems. Barnes left the race in late July. Crowley suspended his campaign in early July, but re-entered after Rodriguez dropped out. Evers has endorsed Crowley.

Attorney General.information:
The attorney general heads the Wisconsin Department of Justice, which provides legal advice and representation, investigates criminal activity, and provides various law enforcement services for the state.
The attorney general is one of three members of the state’s Board of Commissioners of Public Lands along with the secretary of state and the state treasurer.

races.district-race-nutshell: The race for attorney general is a rematch between the incumbent, Democrat Josh Kaul, and Republican Eric Toney, Fond du Lac County’s district attorney. In 2022, Kaul defeated Toney, 50.6% to 49.3%. Kaul won his first four-year term in 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Brad Schimel, 49.4% to 48.8%. Toney was first elected Fond du Lac county’s top prosecutor in 2012.

Lieutenant Gov.information:
The lieutenant governor serves as Wisconsin’s governor when there is a vacancy in the state’s top executive office.
The person takes on duties assigned by the governor, which can include serving on statutory or nonstatutory boards, committees or intergovernmental programs and coordinating state programs.

races.district-race-nutshell: The partisan primary in August gives voters a chance to nominate each party’s candidate for lieutenant governor. The winning candidate from each party forms a joint ticket with their respective gubernatorial nominee in the general election. Will Martin, a consultant from Racine, and David Varnam, a stay-at-home dad from Lancaster, face each other in the Republican primary for lieutenant governor. Martin is endorsed by the Republican Party of Wisconsin. Sarah Godlewski, the current Secretary of State, is unopposed in the Democratic primary for lieutenant governor and will join the ticket of the winner of the Democratic gubernatorial primary.

Treasurer.information:
The treasurer signs checks and oversees the promotion of Wisconsin’s unclaimed property program.
The treasurer is one of three members of the state’s Board of Commissioners of Public Lands along with the attorney general and the secretary of state.

races.district-race-nutshell: Dylan Helmenstine, a Black Earth village board trustee and Wisconsin Heights School Board member, faces Yee Leng Xiong, a Marathon County Supervisor and DC Everest School Board member, in the Democratic primary for state treasurer. The winner of the Aug. 11 election will face incumbent Republican State Treasurer John Leiber in the general election this November.

Secretary of State.information:
The secretary of state is Wisconsin’s official record keeper, which includes keeping track of enrolled laws, resolutions, official acts, fees, positions and appointments. They also maintain the state seal and add it to official acts taken by the governor.
Unlike many other states, the Secretary of State does not administer Wisconsin’s elections. That power lies with local governments and the Wisconsin Elections Commission.
The Secretary of State is one of three members of the state’s Board of Commissioners of Public Lands along with the attorney general and the state treasurer.

races.district-race-nutshell: It's a four-way race in the Republican primary for Secretary of State, which will determine who will advance to the general election in November. The candidates include Brayden Myer of Manitowoc, Nate Pollnow of the Town of Elba, Jay Schroeder of Fox Crossing and Cindy Werner of Milwaukee. Pollnow is endorsed by the Republican Party of Wisconsin. The winner of the Republican primary will face Democrat JoCasta Zamarripa, a Milwaukee alderwoman, and Green Party candidate Pete Karas, a retired small business owner in Muskego. Zamarripa and Karas do not face primary opponents.
